clue.text: Walking out?

definitions.meaning: surface: going for a stroll; cryptically: moving about on foot
surface: outdoors; cryptically: out cold, fast asleep

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are going out for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'out' as unconscious rather than outdoors and the clue describes walking while asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepwalking is the habit of moving about while not awake, which is exactly walking when out cold.

clue.text: Appetiser is more pungent after seconds

indicators.note: after means the word for more pungent comes following the seconds letter

parts.note: tarter means sharper, more acid in taste

explanation.surface: A starter dish turns sharper when you go back for more.
explanation.definitionFit: The first course of a meal is the dish that whets the appetite.

clue.text: Men supporting annual check for car

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting below, so the men come after the check

parts.note: the MOT is the UK's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles
OR means other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Mechanics helping with a car's yearly inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use the word is everyday for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the word is a common informal name for a car.

clue.text: Alimony's first cut admitting mean payment

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the word alimony

parts.note: the opening letter of the word alimony

indicators.note: admitting means the cut word lets the mean word in

parts.note: to lance is to cut open
low means base, mean-spirited

explanation.surface: An ex's maintenance is cut back to a stingy sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular sum paid to someone, such as pocket money or an expense, is a payment.

clue.text: Meat from grouse

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a complaint, or to complain

explanation.surface: A cut of meat taken from a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the bird but is the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names cattle flesh and, informally, a gripe or grumble.

clue.text: Patriot confused about one set up

indicators.note: about means the confused word goes around the rest

parts.note: lost means bewildered

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the words one and set are read from the bottom

parts.note: to lay is to set down

explanation.surface: A bewildered patriot surrounding someone who has been framed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone faithful to king and country is a patriot.

clue.text: Little alternative on board for sailors

indicators.note: on, with board, means sitting aboard, so the alternative goes inside the vessel

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship, and SS is the steamship abbreviation
alt is the short form of alternative

explanation.surface: Sailors have few other options aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on board means being inside a ship, here SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Old salts are experienced seamen, so the plural means sailors.

clue.text: Catch up taking catches in covers

indicators.note: taking means the reversed word holds the other inside
in a down answer, up means the word for catch is read bottom to top

parts.note: to see is to catch on, understand
clips are fastenings, catches

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder makes up ground taking catches in the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like the cricket fielding area; it is the verb: blots out, as the moon does the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: When one body obscures another, as the moon blocks the sun, it hides it from view.

clue.text: Bum support around horse, some say

indicators.note: around means the support word wraps the horse letters

parts.note: to bear is to support

indicators.note: some say means the letters are wanted for how the horse word sounds when spoken

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A backside propped up near a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A bum is also a tramp or vagrant, the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum, in American usage, is a vagrant who begs, a mendicant.

clue.text: Battery is run down in motorway

indicators.note: in tells us the word for run down goes inside the word for motorway

parts.note: an artery is a main road, a major traffic route
run down means unwell, poorly

explanation.surface: A car battery has gone flat while the driver is stuck on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battery' looks like a car part, but it is the military sense: a group of big guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery is a unit of heavy guns, and big guns collectively are the gunnery arm of an army.

clue.text: Largely unclean cash revenue earned, initially

definitions.text: Largely unclean cash revenue earned, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

parts.note: each of these five words gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Money made mostly from dirty dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells the word and describes it: the phrase 'filthy' money is the stock pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means money, especially money gained dishonourably, as in the phrase 'filthy' money.

clue.text: Unseated from chair of state, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a monarch's ceremonial seat is a throne

explanation.surface: A ruler is said to have been removed from power.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a deposed king; the throne only supplies the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who has been unseated by a horse has been tossed off it.

clue.text: Beaming female using whip

parts.note: to lash is to whip; a lashing is a whipping

explanation.surface: A smiling woman wielding a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaming here means shining out light, as a lighthouse or a torch does in bursts.

clue.text: Embarrassed taking pleasure for payback

indicators.note: taking means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment
fun is enjoyment

explanation.surface: Someone shamefacedly having fun as revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid back to a customer is a repayment, so payback in the literal sense.

clue.text: French row, gripping about border

indicators.note: gripping means the French-and-row letters hold the about word

parts.note: a tier is a row or rank
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A French quarrel over a border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary between two countries is their border.

clue.text: Somewhat outclasses sorry judge

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of outclasses into sorry

explanation.surface: A competitor apologises for being a little better than the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who evaluates and values things, such as property or claims, is one who judges them.

clue.text: Revolting retreat over current leader

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a tide is a current

explanation.surface: A rebel withdrawal threatens to topple the current leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a political chief; it is the main opinion article in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article giving its opinion is called the leader.

clue.text: Playboy fellow caught in burglary

indicators.note: caught in means the fellow word sits inside the burglary word

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A rich playboy is nabbed during a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-seeker devoted to enjoyment is the playboy type.

clue.text: Matured, perhaps seeing force reduced

parts.note: lowered means brought down, made less

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a force has been scaled down as things matured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a plant that has bloomed has matured.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossoming is one example of coming to maturity, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Hunt enemy welcoming scrap

indicators.note: welcoming means the enemy word takes the scrap word in

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Searching for an enemy who is up for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight; it is a scrap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food or supplies, i.e. to hunt.

clue.text: Part of girl is somewhat flexible

indicators.note: part of means only a stretch of the following words is used

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of girl through is into somewhat

explanation.surface: A girl is described as fairly supple.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lithe and supple, bending easily.

clue.text: Passion occasionally ardent in pretty pass

indicators.note: in means those letters go inside the pretty pass word

parts.note: a pretty pass is a mess, a sorry state

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of ardent is used

parts.note: taking the first, third and fifth letters of ardent

explanation.surface: Ardent passion now and then leads to a sorry state.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied or wild enthusiasm, as in a passion for something, is a kind of madness.

clue.text: Control straddling old time cycle

indicators.note: straddling means the first word sits on either side of the others

parts.note: to ration is to control the supply of something

explanation.surface: Some control spanning an old period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn round an axis, or a sequence of taking turns, is a cycle.

clue.text: Smell cutting head off fish

indicators.note: cutting head off means removing the first letter of the smell word

parts.note: a stench is a foul smell
the first letter, removed from the front of the smell word

explanation.surface: A beheaded fish gives off a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Fearful person audibly cringed in fear

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: to cower is to shrink back in fear

explanation.surface: A frightened person flinches.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking courage, easily frightened, is a fearful person.

clue.text: Once more putting ace over net

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the ace letter sits above the net word

parts.note: a net figure is a gain or profit

explanation.surface: A tennis player serves an ace over the net again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' looks like the tennis net; it is net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more means a second time, repeated.

clue.text: Worry about Queen being upset

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: Concern that the Queen is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or concern is another name for a worry.

clue.text: Collect last item on shopping list

indicators.note: last item on means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the final letter of the word shopping
to list is to lean, as a ship tilts

explanation.surface: Pick up the final thing on your shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like the shopping list, but it is the verb for a tilting ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, originally leftover grain after harvest.

clue.text: Dull prisoner concealing a nail, oddly

indicators.note: concealing means the prisoner word holds the rest inside

parts.note: an inmate is someone held in a jail
taken as written

indicators.note: oddly means the first and third letters of the word nail

parts.note: taking the first and third letters of nail

explanation.surface: A lifeless convict hides a nail, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless and showing no spirit; dull in the sense of lacking animation.

clue.text: Holds, catching batsman, showing guts

indicators.note: catching means the word for holds goes round the word for batsman

parts.note: clings means holds on tightly
a batsman's job is to hit the ball, so he is a hitter

explanation.surface: A fielder takes a catch to dismiss a batsman, showing bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage; it is literal: the small intestines of a pig, cooked as a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pig intestines prepared as food, so guts in the literal sense.
